summary: Forest Service lookout on Mount Sedgwick in the Zuni Mountains, built 1918 and first staffed by David and Lucy Whiteside; removed in 1975, and no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Removed in 1975 per the register; the New Mexico list marks it gone and no source describes what remains

events.note: Register: first staffed in 1918 by David and Lucy Whiteside. The Cibola Citizen places informal lookout work around 1905 to 1910
Mrs. D.B. Whiteside acted as guard and lookout that year (1920 item quoted by Forest Lookouts)
Forest Service supervisor in touch with the lookout station atop the mountain during fires

June 25, 1939 item (Albuquerque Journal, quoted by Forest Lookouts): Forest Service recently placed emergency lookout guards on the mountain, around the time a fire in the area was believed to have been started by lightning
A lookout at the station helped guide a pilot or crew lost in a heavy rain storm to safety (Gallup Independent, July 20, 1943, quoted by Forest Lookouts)

notes_for_editor: Staffing start is disputed. The register says first staffed in 1918 by the Whitesides; the Cibola Citizen says newspapers suggest informal lookout work around 1905 to 1910 and that Lucy took the post after David's death in March 1919. The story reports both. The 1920 item names the Manzano National Forest, while the register names the Cibola National Forest. No source describes the lookout's design, what remains at the site, or whether the site is open, so facts.access and facts.design are omitted. The brief's record (gone, tower, coordinates, elevation, 1918 and 1975 dates) matches the register; no corrections proposed. The Cibola Citizen article says it revises a July 2025 feature, and its own date is not stated in the text read.
